result.title: Full Fine-Tuning is not the Problem: Why Adam Fails and SGD Succeeds in Few-Shot CLIP Adaptation
result.summary: Few-shot CLIP adaptation is often treated as a parameterization problem. Full fine-tuning is assumed to overfit, so parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) methods are preferred. In this paper, we show that this conclusion conflates parameterization with optimization. Across 11 datasets, 3 CLIP backbones, and 5 shot levels, dense full fine-tuning with plain SGD outperforms representative PEFT methods under the reported evaluation protocol, whereas Adam/AdamW collapses. We trace this collapse to unreliable support-set preconditioning. The few-shot second moment systematically underestimates the corresponding full-data statistic, already at initialization. Adam's inverse-square-root normalization converts this error into an oversized adaptive update. Matching Adam's first-step update budget to SGD resolves most of the collapse, whereas numerator-side alignment does not explain the failure. Shampoo and SOAP also fail, so richer preconditioning alone does not resolve the problem. Theory formalizes how few-shot estimation error is amplified into unsafe updates. SGD succeeds because it avoids unreliable preconditioners and stays close to pretrained CLIP. Interpolation probes show low-loss connections along tested directions, and curvature probes show favorable directional curvature. These results identify optimizer-induced preconditioning, not dense full fine-tuning itself, as the main source of failure in few-shot CLIP adaptation.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在 11 个数据集、3 种 CLIP 骨干和 5 种 shot 设置下发现：少样本全参数微调配 SGD 反而优于代表性 PEFT，而 Adam/AdamW 会崩溃；作者将原因归于少样本二阶矩低估导致的自适应更新过大，并以理论分析和插值、曲率探针佐证。
AI.relevance_reason: 与 LVR 推理期状态生成无直接关联，但其「少样本下 Adam 预条件不可靠」的诊断可供核查：在少量样本上训练 latent 推理适配器或轻量推理模块时，优化器与更新尺度可能同样影响结果。
